Pepper_bell_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is caused by Xanthomonas species and affects pepper plants, causing leaf spots and fruit lesions.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides at first sign of disease
Remove and destroy severely infected plants
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness
Use drip irrigation systems when possible
Apply treatments early morning so leaves dry quickly
Improve air circulation by proper plant spacing
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and transplants
Rotate crops with non-host plants for 2-3 years
Avoid working with plants when leaves are wet
Disinfect tools and equipment between plants
Remove volunteer plants and weeds that may harbor bacteria

Pepper_bell_healthy.description: Healthy bell pepper plant showing vigorous growth with no disease symptoms.
prevention: Regular monitoring for early disease detection

Potato_Early_blight.description: Early blight is caused by Alternaria solani fungus affecting potato plants.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on leaves
Spots appear first on older, lower leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper
Remove and destroy infected plant parts
Improve air circulation by proper spacing
Water at the base of plants to keep foliage dry
Apply mulch to prevent soil splash onto leaves
prevention: Space plants properly for good air circulation
Apply preventive fungicides early in growing season

Potato_Late_blight.description: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans, the same pathogen that caused the Irish Potato Famine.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves that turn brown or black
White fuzzy fungal growth on undersides of leaves
Brown to black lesions on stems
Firm rot on tubers with reddish-brown discoloration
Rapid plant collapse in wet, cool conditions
treatment: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb or chlorothalonil immediately
Remove and destroy infected plants completely
Hill up soil around plants to protect tubers
Harvest tubers during dry weather if possible
prevention: Monitor weather forecasts for blight-favorable conditions
Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles
Space plants adequately for air circulation

Potato_healthy.description: Healthy potato plant with normal growth and development.
treatment: Continue monitoring for pests and diseases

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot caused by Xanthomonas species, a serious disease of tomatoes.
symptoms: Small dark spots with yellow halos on leaves
treatment: Use antibiotics if approved in your region
prevention: Rotate with non-host crops for 2-3 years

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Early blight is caused by Alternaria solani fungus, common in tomato plants.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves
Yellowing and dropping of older leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper
Improve air circulation by staking plants
Water at the base of plants, not overhead
Apply mulch to prevent soil splash
prevention: Rotate crops - don't plant tomatoes in same spot for 3 years
Space plants properly for air circulation
Apply preventive fungicides early in season

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans, devastating to tomatoes and potatoes.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown
White fuzzy growth on undersides of leaves
Rapid plant collapse in humid conditions
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Apply fungicides containing mancozeb or chlorothalonil
Harvest green tomatoes if disease is present
Do not compost infected plant material
prevention: Avoid working with plants when wet
Apply preventive fungicides before symptoms appear

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Leaf mold caused by fungus Passalora fulva, common in greenhouse tomatoes.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown fuzzy growth on undersides

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot caused by fungus Septoria lycopersici.
symptoms: Small circular spots with gray centers and dark borders
Spots appear on lower leaves first
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) in spot centers
Yellowing and dropping of affected leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper
Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Water at soil level, avoid wetting foliage
prevention: Space plants for good air flow
Stake or cage plants to keep off ground
Apply preventive fungicides if disease prone area

Tomato_Spider_mites.description: Spider mites are tiny arachnids that suck plant juices from tomato leaves.
symptoms: Tiny yellow or white spots on leaves (stippling)
Fine webbing on undersides of leaves
Reduced plant vigor and fruit production
treatment: Spray plants with strong water stream to dislodge mites
Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil
Use miticides if infestation is severe
prevention: Avoid water stress (mites thrive in dry conditions)
Monitor plants regularly, especially in hot weather

Tomato_Target_Spot.description: Target spot caused by fungus Corynespora cassiicola.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern)
Spots on leaves, stems, and fruits
treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin
prevention: Apply preventive fungicides in humid conditions

Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: TYLCV is transmitted by whiteflies, causing severe damage to tomatoes.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies
No chemical cure for virus exists
Use yellow sticky traps for monitoring
prevention: Plant during times of low whitefly activity
Use healthy transplants from reliable sources

Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV) causes mottled leaves and reduced yield.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottled pattern on leaves
treatment: Wash hands thoroughly before handling plants
prevention: Purchase certified disease-free seeds and plants
Avoid tobacco products around plants (virus can spread from tobacco)

Tomato_healthy.description: Healthy tomato plant showing vigorous growth and no disease symptoms.

Corn_Cercospora_leaf_spot.description: Cercospora leaf spot caused by fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis.
symptoms: Small rectangular gray spots on leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides if disease is severe
Remove and destroy infected plant debris

Corn_Common_rust.description: Common rust caused by fungus Puccinia sorghi affecting corn plants.
symptoms: Small circular to elongate brown pustules on leaves
Pustules on both sides of leaves
Reddish-brown spores that rub off easily
Severe infections cause premature leaf death
treatment: Apply fungicides if disease is severe
Most hybrid corn has good resistance
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak disease periods

Corn_Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Northern leaf blight caused by fungus Exserohilum turcicum.
symptoms: Long, elliptical gray-green lesions on leaves
Lesions turn tan with dark borders
Lesions grow up to 6 inches long
Severe leaf blighting in susceptible hybrids
Significant yield loss in wet years
treatment: Apply fungicides at first sign of disease
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
prevention: Avoid planting in low, poorly drained areas

Corn_healthy.description: Healthy corn plant with normal growth and development.

Grape_Black_rot.description: Black rot caused by fungus Guignardia bidwellii, serious disease of grapes.
symptoms: Black pycnidia (small dots) in leaf lesions
treatment: Apply fungicides from bud break through harvest
Remove mummified berries from vines and ground
Use systemic fungicides for better control
prevention: Prune vines to improve air circulation
Apply preventive fungicides during wet periods

Grape_Esca.description: Esca is a complex disease caused by multiple fungi affecting grape vines.
symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves (yellow and green bands)
Sudden wilting of shoots in summer
Dark streaking in wood when cut
treatment: Prune out infected wood during dormant season
Remove and destroy infected vine parts
prevention: Maintain vine vigor with proper nutrition

Grape_Leaf_blight.description: Leaf blight caused by fungal pathogens affecting grape leaves.
symptoms: Brown to black spots on leaves

Grape_healthy.description: Healthy grape vine with normal growth and fruit development.

Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis affecting apple trees.
symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown spots on leaves
Velvety or fuzzy appearance on infected areas
Lesions on fruits that become corky and scabby
treatment: Apply fungicides during early spring when leaves emerge
Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits
Prune trees to improve air circulation
Use copper-based fungicides or sulfur sprays
Apply fungicides every 7-10 days during wet weather
prevention: Remove fallen leaves and fruit debris in autumn
Space trees adequately for good air flow
Apply dormant oil sprays in early spring

Apple_Black_rot.description: Black rot caused by fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa affecting apples.
symptoms: Brown spots on leaves with purple margins
Fruit rot starting as small brown spots
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plant parts
Apply fungicides containing captan or myclobutanil
Remove mummified fruits from tree and ground
prevention: Maintain tree vigor with proper fertilization

Apple_Cedar_apple_rust.description: Cedar apple rust caused by fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
treatment: Apply fungicides in spring when orange galls appear
Remove nearby cedar or juniper trees (alternate host)
prevention: Remove cedar trees within 1-2 miles if possible
Apply preventive fungicides from bud break
Maintain tree health with proper care

Apple_healthy.description: Healthy apple tree showing normal growth with no disease symptoms.
prevention: Regular monitoring for early disease detection

Cherry_Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew caused by fungus Podosphaera clandestina on cherry trees.
symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and shoots
prevention: Water at soil level, not overhead

Cherry_healthy.description: Healthy cherry tree with normal growth and fruit production.

Peach_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot caused by Xanthomonas arboricola affecting peach trees.

Peach_healthy.description: Healthy peach tree with normal growth and fruit development.

Strawberry_Leaf_scorch.description: Leaf scorch caused by fungus Diplocarpon earlianum affecting strawberries.

Strawberry_healthy.description: Healthy strawberry plant with normal growth and fruit production.
